title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in PARN-mutant zebrafish
summary: Researchers found expanded hematopoietic stem/progenitor populations and reduced mature blood cells in PARN-loss zebrafish; cholesterol-pathway inhibition rescued expansion and anemia, and cholesterol-pathway activation was also observed in patient-derived iPSCs. Ilastik interactive machine learning generated image probability maps, followed by CellProfiler/Otsu segmentation, to quantify blood-lineage staining and cell counts supporting the phenotype and treatment comparisons. This AI role concerned image-based measurement; pathway identification and rescue conclusions also relied on experimental and transcriptomic assays. The treatment findings remain preclinical, and the iPSC observations do not establish patient benefit.
ai_technology: Ilastik interactive machine learning for bioimage analysis
organization: CHEO Research Institute; University of Ottawa

evidence.tested: Ilastik probability maps plus CellProfiler segmentation were used to quantify WISH/o-dianisidine staining and distinguish labeled-cell counts in zebrafish hematopoietic phenotyping; biological rescue results were experimentally tested in PARN-loss zebrafish and pathway activation was recapitulated in patient-derived iPSCs.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed Image analyses Methods: the incremental effect of ML segmentation versus manual/non-ML quantification. Clinical treatment benefit is not established by the zebrafish rescue and patient-derived iPSC experiments.
evidence.ai_role: Interactive ML image segmentation measured stained/fluorescent blood-lineage markers and cell counts that support the PARN-mutant hematopoietic phenotype; it was not used to identify the cholesterol pathway.

source_review.scope: Publisher article abstract; selected hematopoietic phenotype, cholesterol/rescue Results; Image analyses Methods; author affiliations. Supplementary material was not reviewed.
